Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-08
Time: 16:00 UTC (local times: SF 09:00, LDN 16:00)
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sarah Lopez (Helios - Procurement), Anand Rao (Helios - Head of Security), Priya Menon (Helios - Legal Counsel), Tom Bradford (Helios - CTO)

Auto-generated summary: Redwood and Helios aligned on a pilot path; legal to redline DPA; pricing spreadsheet to be shared; tech deep dive on KMS/VPC next week.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on a late afternoon. I think we have about 45, 50 minutes, so i'll run quick agenda, then hand to Liam for the technical bits and then we'll take questions. quick agenda; DPA redline readout, SLA and pricing decision paths, and pilot scope.
[00:22] Sarah Lopez: Sounds good. we've got Priya and Anand on to cover legal and security.. and Tom to speak to ops. so we're primarily focused on the exceptions in the DPA and cost impacts.
[00:30] Tom Bradford: yep, high level we'd like minimal vendor-managed keying; we prefer customer key control if possible. also the SLA metrics - we need p95 under 200ms for our user flows, and an escalation path.
[00:45] Liam O'Connor: got it. quick flag — our Dedicated product can meet tight p95 latency in most cases, depending on sequence lengths and batching. There's trade-offs between throughput/cost; continuous batching can push down price but increase tail.
[01:05] Anand Rao: On the KMS piece, we need to know whether Redwood supports Bring-Your-Own-Key to a customer-managed KMS (like AWS KMS or external HSM). Also audit logs and key rotation policies need to be explicit.
[01:20] Maya Chen: absolutely. on BYOK, we do support customer-managed keys for Redwood Private and in some Dedicated setups — i'll let Liam walk through exact modes. For hosted API there's an escrow/tenant-level key but we can discuss authorized access controls.
[01:36] Liam O'Connor: (slight pause) ok so there are three common patterns we see: 1) Hosted: Redwood manages keys (fastest time to value), 2) Dedicated with customer KMS integration — Redwood stores encrypted model assets and you keep the key in your KMS, 3) Private deploy (VPC/on-prem) where customer controls the key entirely. important note — some of our older doc references call it "Redwood Dedicated" or 'red wood dedicate' in the transcript — ignore that, it's the same product.
[02:10] Priya Menon: on the DPA redlines we proposed two non-standard clauses: a narrow audit right for crypto key handling, and limitation of data use to operational troubleshooting only, with a short retention window. we also asked for indemnity carveouts for regulated data.
[02:30] Maya Chen: thanks Priya. two quick comments: for audit rights we can offer SOC-2 and ISO artifacts in lieu of broad live audits; for data use we have strict production telemetry controls and are open to a retention window. indemnity is something we escalate to legal; we can surface standard playbooks or limited carveouts but need to confirm with contracts.
[02:55] Sarah Lopez: timeline wise procurement needs pricing approval by April 17 to hit finance cycle. so getting the pricing sheet and committed usage options is critical.
[03:07] Maya Chen: understood. our commercial path: we can propose a committed reserved capacity for Dedicated (monthly commit) with an egress discount schedule. alternatively, a short pilot with a credit and consumption billing then convert to commit if metrics hit. i'll include both options on the pricing sheet.
[03:25] Tom Bradford: ballpark, what's the difference in unit cost between hosted and dedicated with a 12-month commit? rough numbers are fine.
[03:35] Maya Chen: rough rule of thumb: Dedicated with a 12-month commitment can be 25-40% lower unit cost depending on utilization and quantization options. if you run heavy embedding workloads we can optimize with caching and quantized weights to push cost lower.
[03:55] Anand Rao: who manages the KV cache and any potential leakage? we need assurance around prefix caching not exposing PII across tenants.
[04:06] Liam O'Connor: good question. our runtime uses per-tenant KV cache with strict isolation; for Dedicated we can configure caching policies and TTLs. there are enterprise modes that disable prefix caching entirely for sensitive workloads. i can bring the cache config doc in the tech follow-up.
[04:25] Priya Menon: can we get explicit language for data residency and deletion? our compliance team requires a contractual deletion timeline after contract termination.
[04:35] Maya Chen: yes we can add a deletion SLA in the DPA. standard is 30 days, but we can discuss faster windows for regulated datasets.
[04:44] Sarah Lopez: okay great. on the MSA exceptions — Priya highlighted the auditor rights and indemnity; are there any other commercial asks?
[04:52] Priya Menon: also clause around subcontractors and where data may be processed; Helios has a strict list of allowed regions.
[05:00] Maya Chen: we can enumerate subprocessors and region restrictions; we'll include our current cloud regions and a commitment to notify on changes.
[05:08] Tom Bradford: switching to SLA details — we need an uptime SLA (monthly) with financial credits and a technical escalation path. how does Redwood typically specify credits?
[05:20] Liam O'Connor: standard template is credits based on monthly availability tiers: <99.9% etc. for Dedicated we can offer improved uptime targets per contract. community note: sometimes the SLA conversation becomes more of a commercial negotiation than a technical one.
[05:40] Sarah Lopez: procurement usually wants a hard SLA with clear remediation steps; finance cares about credit structure. so if you can show both an engineering escalation matrix and a credit table that will speed review.
[05:55] Maya Chen: we'll provide both: an engineer-on-call escalation ladder and a simple credits table in the commercial term sheet.
[06:03] Anand Rao: about SSO and RBAC: we need SAML/SCIM support and fine-grained RBAC for token and key access. can Redwood integrate with our identity provider?
[06:14] Liam O'Connor: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported; tokens can be scoped per route/model and RBAC roles map to key operations. there are some edge cases with service account key rotation, i'll itemize them in the deep-dive.
[06:30] Priya Menon: on the DPA redline you had a section 'data processor obligations' that still sounds broad. can you confirm that Redwood will not use customer data for model training or improvement?
[06:44] Maya Chen: yes, we enforce a policy: customer data will not be used for model training unless explicitly opted-in. we'll make that explicit in the DPA and add a contractual clause to that effect.
[06:58] Tom Bradford: good. any latitude on the data retention for logs? 30 days is okay but what about forensic logs for incidents — can those be 90 days?
[07:10] Anand Rao: we prefer 90 days for security logs, but redwood should limit content to metadata not PII.
[07:18] Maya Chen: we can propose split retention: operational logs 30 days, security forensic logs 90 days, all redacted for PII by default. i'll capture that.
[07:27] Sarah Lopez: back to pricing — can you share examples or references of other fintech customers with similar commit profiles? redwood previously referenced a 'billing reference' — would be helpful to see anonymized case studies.
[07:40] Maya Chen: i can provide anonymized references and an example price curve. i'll be careful on customer confidentiality but can share percent savings and utilization assumptions.
[07:51] Priya Menon: another legal item — export control and regulated data clause. Helios operates in EU and APAC; we need data residency guarantees for certain product lines.
[08:02] Liam O'Connor: tech wise we can pin instances to region and use regional GPU pools. some crates on older docs mention 'KV cash' or 'K V cash' which is transcription artifacts — the technical design will be crisp in the follow-up.
[08:20] Maya Chen: quick pause — any blockers to schedule the tech deep-dive next week? Anand indicated availability and Liam is ok. we can lock 60 minutes to go through connectivity diagrams, KMS flows, and a pilot runbook.
[08:32] Anand Rao: yes week of April 14 works. prefer mornings PST.
[08:38] Tom Bradford: from ops side i want a runbook that includes rollback and fallback to hosted model if dedicated pilot has issues. basically we need graceful degradation and a fall-back route.
[08:50] Liam O'Connor: we have a routing policy that can cascade to hosted variants; for pilot we'll propose a canary route and fallback plan in the runbook.
[09:00] Sarah Lopez: procurement timeline recap: get pricing and commit options by April 10, legal redlines by April 17, then final approval week of April 21 to hit finance.
[09:12] Maya Chen: summary — Maya will send pricing, SOW, and a commercial term sheet; Liam will prepare technical diagrams and caching/KMS options; Helios legal will prioritize redlines. agreed?
[09:22] Priya Menon: yes. one practical question: in the DPA we asked for deletion confirmation within 7 days for a subset of regulated flows — is that feasible?
[09:33] Maya Chen: 7 days is aggressive but for a scoped data type we can commit to expedited deletion; i'll flag that for contracts and ops and see what the implementation window looks like.
[09:45] Tom Bradford: can you also include a short section on performance testing methodology? we'd like to run an apples-to-apples benchmark using our prompt sets.
[09:55] Liam O'Connor: absolutely. we'll pair on the benchmark harness; typically we capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. we can run with both quantized and FP16 variants.
[10:08] Sarah Lopez: any competitors in play? we're evaluating other vendors for latency and cost.
[10:14] Maya Chen: we know customers also look at OpenAI and Anthropic for hosted, and Bedrock for region-specific needs. Redwood's differentiation is the unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and the operational tooling for rollouts — but we'll leave that to the POC to show.
[10:30] Priya Menon: last legal thing — we need an IP clause that clarifies derived outputs ownership for user content. Helios wants clear ownership of outputs generated from their data.
[10:42] Maya Chen: we can add a clause: customer owns outputs generated from their prompts; Redwood retains model IP and tooling. we'll make that explicit in the MSA.
[10:51] Anand Rao: ok i'm going to quickly list the tech items we want in the follow-up: KMS key flow diagrams, VPC peering vs Private link options, RBAC token scoping, cache config and disabled cache mode, and benchmark harness.
[11:05] Liam O'Connor: noted. i'll prepare a deck and a network diagram, and we'll attach the benchmark scripts.
[11:15] Sarah Lopez: procurement needs a single line item for the finance system: recurring monthly amount and estimated egress. please include a conservative egress estimate and a capped-escrow option if possible.
[11:28] Maya Chen: will do. i'll include a conservative egress bucket and an optional capped egress add-on for the first 3 months.
[11:36] Tom Bradford: last thing — can we get a sample MSA excerpt that shows the escalation ladder and SLA credits? our legal team wants to see the precise language before redlining.
[11:48] Maya Chen: yes i'll push a sample MSA extract with the SLA and credits table.
[11:55] Sarah Lopez: great. thanks everyone.
[12:00] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll recap next steps in email.
